record.paper_title: Geometric curvature energies: facts, trends, and open problems
record.original_question: For higher-dimensional geometric curvature energies on submanifolds, including higher-dimensional integral Menger curvature and tangent-point energy, what are the Euler-Lagrange equations, can one prove higher regularity for local minimizers or critical points, and what variational inclusions should replace Euler-Lagrange equations for the nonsmooth geometric energies obtained by replacing some of the integrations with maximizations? The same block also asks what regularity can be proved for thick knotted surfaces that minimize area.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $1\le k<d$ be integers and let $\Sigma=\Sigma^k\subset\mathbb{R}^d$ be a $k$-dimensional $\mathcal{H}^k$-measurable submanifold (sufficiently smooth where required). Consider the following geometric curvature energies:

(i) The higher-dimensional tangent-point energy of exponent $p>0$:
$$E_p(\Sigma)\;=\;\int_\Sigma\!\!\int_\Sigma \frac{1}{R_{\mathrm{tp}}(x,y)^p}\,d\mathcal{H}^k(x)\,d\mathcal{H}^k(y),$$
where $R_{\mathrm{tp}}(x,y)$ is the radius of the smallest $d$-dimensional ball tangent to $T_x\Sigma$ at $x$ and passing through $y$.

(ii) The higher-dimensional integral Menger curvature of exponent $p>0$:
$$M_p(\Sigma)\;=\;\int_\Sigma\!\cdots\!\int_\Sigma K_p(x_0,\dots,x_{k+1})\,d\mathcal{H}^k(x_0)\cdots d\mathcal{H}^k(x_{k+1}),$$
the integration being over $(k+2)$ copies of $\Sigma$, where $K_p(x_0,\dots,x_{k+1})$ equals the reciprocal $p$-th power of the circumradius (or equivalent geometric size) of the $(k+1)$-simplex spanned by the points $x_0,\dots,x_{k+1}$.

(iii) Non-smooth variants of these energies obtained by replacing one or more of the integrations in (i) or (ii) by a supremum over the corresponding variable (e.g. $\sup_{y\in\Sigma}\int_\Sigma R_{\mathrm{tp}}(x,y)^{-p}\,d\mathcal{H}^k(x)$, or $\sup_{x_0,\dots,x_j}\int\!\cdots\!\int K_p\,d\mathcal{H}^k(x_{j+1})\cdots$, and analogous mixed forms).

Solve the following:

(a) Derive the Euler–Lagrange equations for $E_p$ and for $M_p$ on smooth $k$-dimensional submanifolds for $k\ge 2$, identifying the leading-order operator and lower-order terms.

(b) Prove higher regularity of local minimizers and of critical points of $E_p$ and $M_p$ for appropriate ranges of $p$ above the scale-invariant exponent (e.g. establish $C^\infty$ or analytic regularity by a bootstrap argument).

(c) For the non-smooth variants in (iii), formulate the appropriate variational inclusions (subdifferential or measure-valued first-order conditions) that replace the Euler–Lagrange equations, and study their structure.

(d) Establish regularity results for "thick knotted surfaces" minimizing area among $k$-dimensional surfaces in $\mathbb{R}^d$ subject to a uniform thickness (positive reach / lower bound on $R_{\mathrm{tp}}$) constraint within a fixed isotopy class.
artifact.status_search_result: Available results address the Euler–Lagrange equations and $C^\infty$-regularity of critical points only in the one-dimensional (curve) case, e.g. Blatt–Reiter's regularity theory for tangent-point energies $TP^{(p,2)}$ and integral Menger curvature $\mathrm{int}M^{(p,2)}$ on curves. The higher-dimensional analogues (Euler–Lagrange equations on $k$-submanifolds for $k\ge 2$, higher regularity of minimizers/critical points, variational inclusions for the sup-versions, and regularity of thick area-minimizing knotted surfaces) do not appear to have been resolved in the literature, and remain stated as open problems.

status_evidence.title: Regularity theory for tangent-point energies: The non-degenerate sub-critical case
status_evidence.snippet: Stationary points of TP^(p,2)+λ length, p∈(4,5), are smooth (curves).
status_evidence.claim: Regularity is established for curves; higher-dimensional case not covered.

status_evidence.title: Tangent-Point Repulsive Potentials for a Class of Non-smooth m-dimensional Sets in R^n
status_evidence.snippet: Self-avoidance and smoothing effects for higher-dimensional tangent-point energies established for suitable exponents.
status_evidence.claim: Higher-dimensional results focus on self-avoidance and Sobolev-Slobodeckij regularity, not on Euler-Lagrange equations or full smoothness of critical points.

status_evidence.title: Publications of Simon Blatt
status_evidence.snippet: List of papers focused predominantly on one-dimensional knot energies and their regularity.
status_evidence.claim: No publication establishing Euler-Lagrange equations and higher regularity for k-dimensional integral Menger or tangent-point energies for k≥2.
